data.name: The Visitor
data.detailed_description:
The Visitor is a VR ONLY horror experience about an unexpected visitor calling to your door in the middle of the night. The game relies heavily on atmosphere, utilizing a dark environment to make the player both as nervous and uncomfortable as possible. The Visitor does not require any controls. Visual cues such as flickering lights inform the player of where to direct their gaze, so simply put on your VR headset and enjoy.

What does The Visitor run on?

  • HTC Vive
  • Rift CV1 (Please read the discussion titled "Running on CV1" if you are using the CV1)
  • Oculus Rift 1.3.0 or above

Why The Visitor?

  • Ideal VR experience for scaring friends and family.
  • It is a great introduction to VR
  • Only takes 10-12 minutes to complete, so scaring a friends is quick and easy
  • No controls required (just a headset), so don't worry about not being familiar with game controls

Gameplay Mechanics

The Visitor was made with the intention of being as accessible as possible, so because of that, absolutely no controls are required. You just need to put on the headset, look around, and enjoy :)

reviews.review:
There seems to be a clear split on this game. One thing I noticed is that the more recent reviews are more negative, and the older ones are positive. I have a theory as to why. People that bought this game recently are probably now acustomed to more fleshed out horror games like Dreadhalls or something , and so they probably wouldnt find this scary, and will be quick to label it as too short, or "cheaply produced". Those people are idiots, and looking at their other reviews just backs that up.

The dev mentions that this game is SHORT and a good INTRODUCTION TO VR, yet people are complaining that its not a masterpiece. The dev openly admits that this was a learning process, and proceeds are funding a more interactive game. He was kind enough to send me some screenshots via Reddit too. 

First off, I thoroughly enjoyed the game, as I could just sit back, not worry about controls, and enjoy a bit of tension. No it isnt as scary as fully fledged horrors, but I didnt pay 15 euro for it, so I wont complain. The ending leaves me wanting a bit more, but that is a constructive criticism.

Why you should buy this game:
- It is really handy to just put it on to show a friend or a relative that wouldnt be comfortable to use controls
- Because it is so short, it isn't tedious watching a friend play through it.
- You want to support devs. This is clearly a learning process, and the dev has said that proceeds are going towards a more interactive version. The screenshots he sent me from his second game already shoe that he has learned a lot and has at the very least, improved the game graphically.

Do not buy it if :
- You expect a masterpiece for 0.99c
- You expect a work of art from a dev that openly says this is his first VR experience, and was a learning experience 
- You are expecting Paranormal Activity VR 
- You have played more advanced horror games and are expecting something like those.

Sometimes I pity devs that have to endure stupid reviews. I swear, some of these people would buy a Fiat and complain its not a Porche.
